text:
alex: Ran an nsys capture for the TRT+vLLM end-to-end path. Weird: wrapper time looks huge compared to engine exec. Posting top-level observations first.

maria: Share the capture/command?

alex: ran `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=trt_vllm_run` on a 4-GPU node. timeline shows repeated host->device memcpy spikes that align with wrapper boundary.

sven: timeline screenshot? are kernels short and frequent or a few long kernels?

alex: lots of short kernels. Bulk of GPU time split: 31% wrapper (memcpy + enqueue), 18% engine->execute_async, 12% kernel compute, 25% small kernel launches and driver overhead, rest idle.

jessica: that suggests scheduling/batching is fragmenting work. vLLM may be flushing KV per request. Any KV copy traces?

alex: yes, the wrapper copies KV shards into a staging buffer before every inference step:

```
# pseudocode from wrapper trace
for token in generation:
  cudaMemcpyAsync(dst_stage, kv_segment, size, stream)
  enqueueEngine(execution_context)
  cudaStreamSynchronize(stream)  # sometimes shows up as blocking
```

This shows up as repeated small memcpys in the nsys timeline.

perf-bot: automated-summary: wrapper_memcpy=31%, engine_launch=18%, nvtx_waits=9%, cpu_spin_lock=7%

tim: vLLM scheduler could be creating tiny batches (size=1) because of batching heuristic config. We saw that before when latency-SLO trimming was aggressive.

maria: can you dump the scheduler metrics (batch size distribution)?

alex: attaching quick stats from the run: batch_sizes: [1: 64%, 2: 18%, 4+: 18%] ; avg latency 210ms; p95 410ms. After forcing max_batch_tokens higher the distribution shifts.

sven: strong signal. When batches are size 1, KV copying per token is amortized poorly. Also TRT kernel selection can matter: if kernel selector picks a variant that requires extra prolog copies, that shows up as memcpy overhead.

jessica: idea: aggregate KV copies per batch instead of per token. Or preallocate contiguous KV and use pointer swaps. Might eliminate many cudaMemcpy calls.

alex: sanity-check commands I'm going to run next:

```
# capture kernels + nvtx around scheduler
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --output=trt_vllm_schedule \
  --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite -- 
  ./run_inference --enable-nvtx

# perfetto for CPU stacks + NVTX (longer)
perfetto --background -o /tmp/trace.perfetto --config my_perfetto_config.pbtxt
```

maria: also try forcing TensorRT kernel variant via env var / override. We have an old selector map `TRT_KERNEL_OVERRIDE` to force fp16_smem variant in tests. Compare nvprof kernel durations with and without.

sven: I ran a forced-variant test earlier: switching kernel variant dropped driver launch overhead by ~40% and removed a memcpy prolog. End-to-end latency went from ~220ms -> ~150ms on same workload.

jessica: good. But we need to validate accuracy/regressions after forcing variant. Also check cache warmup: KV cache hit pattern matters too — if vLLM is re-allocating KV per request we should be seeing repeated allocations in the CPU timeline.

perf-bot: note: previous deploy (2026-02-12) had a similar wrapper spike but at lower scale; regression introduced after scheduler backpressure change.

alex: I instrumented the wrapper: adding NVTX push/pop around memcpy and engine->enqueue. In the trace the NVTX bands show memcpy+sync blocks serializing the GPU.

tim: can we overlap memcpy with compute more aggressively? Maybe use double-buffered KV staging and rotate streams. Also remove synchronous stream syncs.

sven: yeah. Two quick experiments: 1) turn memcpy -> cudaMemcpyAsync on separate stream and don't sync; 2) coalesce multiple small memcpys into single large copy per batch. Both cut wrapper time.

maria: please run experiment 1 and 2 and attach numbers (avg/p95 latency + GPU util). If 2 reduces driver calls significantly that's a clear win.

alex: running experiment 1 now. Early result: avg latency down 180ms, p95 240ms, wrapper down to 18%. GPU util up ~12%.

jessica: solid. For production we should: update wrapper to batch KV copies, add a scheduling hint to avoid issuing tiny batches (bump min_batch_size or introduce microbatcher), and add an automated perf-test in CI that runs a short perfetto capture checking for >20% wrapper time.

alex: opened a small PR draft with NVTX markers and a toggle for coalesced-copies. Linking after tests.

maria: ping @sven and @tim to review the PR, especially the streaming changes. We'll also run a canary on Dedicated.

sven: will review. Also let's add a test that forces a different TRT kernel variant and validates latency vs. accuracy.

alex: I'll post the perfetto + nsys links here once uploads finish. Thanks all for quick triage, this feels actionable. :thumbsup:
